state: Updated 2026-10-20: P2 code findings PP-REV-001, PP-REV-002, PP-REV-003, and PP-REV-006 are resolved in source with fresh automated tests; P1 architectural/hardware gates remain explicit boundaries.

findings.title: Contradictory workspace flags select Demo implicitly
findings.runtime_status: Resolved in source and verified by 11 parameterized unit test cases (E-020).
findings.observation: WorkspaceLaunchSelector.Select now parses --real-workspace, --demo-workspace, --demo, and GETSEEK_POS_DEMO before window bootstrap. Any combination of two or more explicit CLI workspace flags returns WorkspaceLaunchMode.ConflictingFlags, logs WORKSPACE_FLAG_CONFLICT, presents the startup error screen, and opens no database or worker.

options.title: Reject contradictory workspace flags (recommended)
options.tradeoff: Adds an explicit startup error for ambiguous scripts.
steps: Add a single workspace argument parser before creating the window.
Reject conflicting explicit workspace selectors; preserve each valid selector.
Use the parsed workspace for title, logging, bootstrap and worker selection.
acceptance: Table-driven tests for all flag combinations and GETSEEK_POS_DEMO precedence.
Verify invalid flags open no database and start no worker.

options.title: Keep and document Demo precedence
options.tradeoff: Small change; conflicting launch scripts remain ambiguous.
steps: Document the existing precedence in launcher configuration.
Add regression tests for the precedence and window identity.
acceptance: Verify the chosen database, title and worker state for each combination.

options.title: Replace flags with one workspace option
options.tradeoff: Clear long-term interface; needs launcher compatibility work.
steps: Introduce --workspace real|demo|preview.
Provide a deprecation path for existing flags.
Update launchers and documented examples together.
acceptance: Compatibility tests and an explicit invalid-value error.

findings.rollback: Revert the parser/launcher changes together; do not migrate or reset any workspace.
findings.source_refresh_note: 2026-10-23: referenced test source inspected; historical E-020 results were not rerun in this import-only verification.

findings.title: Pre-transaction pipeline failures use a different error path
findings.runtime_status: Resolved in source and verified by injected preflight fault/cancellation unit tests (E-020).
findings.observation: CommandPipeline.ExecuteAsync wraps all post-gate preflight operations (permission resolution, module license check, clock-tamper check, canonical hash serialization, optimistic idempotency check, and BeginTransactionAsync) inside the unified cancellation/exception boundary. Rollback is invoked only when tx is not null, and the execution gate is always released in finally.

options.title: Normalize failures at the pipeline boundary (recommended)
options.tradeoff: Makes callers consistent; transaction state must remain precise.
steps: Define an outer cancellation/exception boundary for all asynchronous preflight work.
Track whether a transaction began; roll back only an active transaction.
Keep one sanitized diagnostic ID and preserve finally-based gate release.
acceptance: Inject resolver, license, clock, idempotency-read and transaction-start failures.
Assert no duplicate command execution, correct cancellation result, released gate and no leaked transaction.

options.title: Keep exception ownership in every caller
options.tradeoff: Avoids pipeline restructuring; every consumer must honor the same contract.
steps: Document which failures may throw.
Audit each UI/service caller and centralize safe error reporting.
Add consumer contract tests.
acceptance: Failure injection for each distinct consumer and user-visible safe message.

options.title: Introduce typed preflight failures
options.tradeoff: More explicit diagnostics; larger API change.
steps: Define preflight failure categories and stable safe codes.
Adapt ports and pipeline to convert known operational failures.
Retain a final boundary for unexpected failures.
acceptance: Cancellation, storage-busy, storage-unavailable and unexpected-exception cases.

findings.rollback: Revert the error-boundary/API change; preserve existing transaction and idempotency semantics.
findings.source_refresh_note: 2026-10-23: referenced test source inspected; historical E-020 results were not rerun in this import-only verification.

findings.title: Worker-level failures can repeat without a diagnostic
findings.runtime_status: Resolved in source and verified by worker cycle deduplication unit test (E-020).
findings.observation: OutputDeviceWorker accepts an optional cycleErrorLogger callback (wired in App.axaml.cs to PosBootstrapper.LogDiagnosticError) and deduplicates contiguous pre-claim cycle exceptions by exception type and message signature, resetting the signature after any healthy cycle.

options.title: Add bounded worker diagnostics (recommended)
options.tradeoff: Preserves recovery; needs deduplication to avoid flooding.
steps: Inject a sanitized worker diagnostic sink.
Report pre-claim failures with a stable context and deduplicate repeated errors.
Record recovery and expose worker health without automatically retrying drawer output.
acceptance: Inject connection/settings/transition failures and assert a bounded diagnostic plus recovery.
Assert no extra claim, print or drawer pulse is caused by logging.

options.title: Add durable worker health and backoff
options.tradeoff: Better operator visibility; adds persistence and lifecycle complexity.
steps: Define healthy/degraded/recovering worker states.
Persist the last safe error reference and bounded retry timing.
Expose an operator view and recovery probe.
acceptance: State-transition tests, restart recovery and no secret payloads in health records.

options.title: Stop the loop and let a supervisor restart it
options.tradeoff: Central supervision; restart policy must respect uncertain physical outcomes.
steps: Define fatal versus transient worker errors.
Report fatal errors to the owner process.
Use bounded restarts and preserve startup outcome-unknown recovery.
acceptance: Restart loop limits and receipt/drawer uncertainty recovery tests.

findings.rollback: Disable the new health/logging integration while retaining existing uncertain-output handling.
findings.source_refresh_note: 2026-10-23: referenced test source inspected; historical E-020 results were not rerun in this import-only verification.

findings.title: DataService contracts do not establish Desktop cutover
findings.runtime_status: Not installed, started or exercised during this review.
findings.observation: Desktop bootstrap composes direct LocalAppData SQLite access. DataService separately owns ProgramData workspaces. The router implements selected setup, authentication and read operations, while other typed contracts return SERVICE_ENDPOINT_NOT_READY. A full service-owned checkout/import/export path must not be presented as complete.

options.title: Keep the current boundary explicit (recommended now)
options.tradeoff: Documentation correction only; service cutover remains future work.
steps: Document Desktop and service stores as separate runtime profiles.
List implemented routes and unavailable contracts.
Require an ownership and migration decision before claiming a cutover.
acceptance: Review launch/configuration evidence and a route capability matrix.

options.title: Plan an incremental service cutover
options.tradeoff: Larger engineering program requiring isolated fixtures and migration controls.
steps: Select one vertical workflow and define data ownership.
Implement live session/permission checks, transaction/audit/idempotency and projections.
Cut over only after migration, failure and rollback rehearsals.
acceptance: End-to-end isolated fixture tests, stale token/permission revocation, disconnect/retry and migration rollback.

options.title: Defer service distribution
options.tradeoff: Simpler deployment surface; explicitly limits the service capability.
steps: Mark unsupported contracts unavailable in all product-facing material.
Keep direct Desktop operations as the documented supported profile pending owner confirmation.
acceptance: Packaging review ensures no promise of completed service-owned operations.

findings.rollback: For a future cutover, restore the prior application profile only under an approved data migration/backup plan; documentation changes alone move no data.

findings.title: Physical output remains a separate acceptance gate
findings.runtime_status: No printer, drawer, paper, DPI or multilingual hardware checks performed.
findings.observation: The worker records SpoolAccepted, OutcomeUnknown and NeedsOperatorReview. Spool acceptance does not prove a physical receipt or correct drawer action. The source has dedicated thermal confirmation commands; do not replace physical verification with a successful queue submission.

options.title: Run an isolated physical acceptance matrix (recommended)
options.tradeoff: Requires operator time and test hardware.
steps: Prepare synthetic receipts and a test printer/drawer profile.
Test Thai/Myanmar glyphs, geometry, missing/offline device, cancellation and restart uncertainty.
Record model, driver, paper, DPI, observations and diagnostic references.
acceptance: Physical samples and operator sign-off for each supported profile; no automatic uncertain drawer replay.

options.title: Support only profiles with existing physical evidence
options.tradeoff: Restricts advertised hardware until evidence exists.
steps: Inventory actual approved hardware evidence.
Limit support claims to reviewed profiles.
Mark all other profiles unverified in configuration guidance.
acceptance: Every claimed profile links to dated physical evidence.

options.title: Keep output disabled in evaluation environments
options.tradeoff: Avoids unintended physical action; does not validate production printing.
steps: Use a synthetic workspace and disabled output profile.
Review queued state changes without dispatching a device.
acceptance: Confirm no worker physical output and retain the outstanding hardware gate.

findings.rollback: Restore the previous reviewed output profile; retain job history and inspect uncertain output before reprinting.

findings.title: Historical passing tests omit excluded files
findings.runtime_status: Audited excluded files; active single-register bootstrapper tests restored and executed (7 passed in E-021).
findings.observation: The three Compile Remove entries in GetSeek.IntegrationTests.csproj target retired pre-migration-068 multi-terminal identity transfer APIs (TransferTerminalIdentityAsync / TerminalId). The active single-register production bootstrapper assertions (clean startup, persisted catalog/decimals, safe error masking, currency/precision validation, and restart durability) are compiled and verified in SingleRegisterProductionBootstrapperTests.cs.

options.title: Review exclusions and design focused probes (recommended)
options.tradeoff: Requires a later authorized application test workspace.
steps: Read the exclusion reasons and map each omitted scenario to current behavior.
Choose focused replacement or repaired tests.
Run in a separate disposable test checkout with synthetic databases.
acceptance: Report included/excluded tests separately and attach fresh test evidence.

options.title: Repair and restore excluded tests
options.tradeoff: Potentially stronger regression coverage; effort depends on obsolete fixtures.
steps: Update obsolete setup and expected contracts.
Remove exclusions only after the scenarios are valid.
Run focused and appropriate broader checks in isolation.
acceptance: Compilation includes the files and meaningful assertions pass.

options.title: Retain exclusions with explicit coverage debt
options.tradeoff: Lowest immediate effort; leaves known evidence gaps.
steps: Record the owner, rationale and replacement verification for each excluded file.
Keep historical totals clearly dated.
acceptance: No feature acceptance claim relies solely on the historical total.

findings.rollback: Revert test-only changes in their future isolated checkout; leave production data untouched.

findings.title: Recovery executable is a placeholder
findings.runtime_status: The entire two-line Program.cs was inspected; executable was not run.
findings.observation: GetSeek.Recovery/Program.cs contains only the template Hello, World output. The project does not implement a recovery workflow. Its presence must not be treated as backup, repair, restore or privileged service-recovery capability.

options.title: Exclude recovery capability from support claims (recommended now)
options.tradeoff: Accurate present boundary; an operational recovery procedure still needs separate evidence.
steps: Mark the executable as a placeholder in technical and packaging documentation.
Identify the actual supported backup/restore procedure and evidence, if one exists.
Exclude the placeholder from any promised recovery acceptance.
acceptance: No release or support document presents the template as working recovery.

options.title: Design a separate recovery implementation
options.tradeoff: Substantial engineering and operational validation.
steps: Define data ownership, operator identity, offline/online restrictions and backup format.
Design dry-run, integrity checks, safe restoration and rollback.
Implement only in an isolated application checkout with synthetic recovery fixtures.
acceptance: Interrupted restore, invalid backup, wrong workspace and permissions tests; documented recovery rehearsal.

options.title: Plan removal from distributed packaging
options.tradeoff: Simplifies the package; requires checking references and installer expectations.
steps: Inventory installer and tool references.
Remove the placeholder from a future application distribution.
Update support instructions.
acceptance: Packaging validation and no broken tool references.

findings.rollback: Documentation-only classification moves no data. Future packaging or recovery changes require their own rollback and restore rehearsal.

findings.title: Kitchen ticket producers have no bundled worker claim route
findings.runtime_status: Producer and worker claim SQL inspected; no order, printer or external consumer exercised.
findings.observation: SendOrderToKitchenCommand records SentToKitchen and enqueues KitchenTicket. Cancellation can enqueue KitchenTicketCancel. OutputDeviceWorker.ClaimAsync selects only ReceiptPrint, DrawerKick and ShelfLabelPrint. The source search found no other kitchen-ticket consumer under Software/src. Queueing a kitchen ticket therefore does not establish a bundled kitchen-print route. The current Cafe UI uses pay-now Counter Service; backend/legacy order handlers must be documented separately.

options.title: Document the queue-only/legacy boundary (recommended now)
options.tradeoff: Documentation correction; does not implement kitchen output.
steps: Describe current Cafe counter checkout separately from backend order handlers.
Label KitchenTicket and cancellation jobs as lacking a bundled consumer.
Verify any separately deployed consumer before making kitchen-output claims.
acceptance: No guide equates SentToKitchen or queued jobs with a physical kitchen print.

options.title: Plan and implement a kitchen-output consumer
options.tradeoff: Requires application engineering, device policy and physical acceptance.
steps: Define ticket/cancellation payload versions and printer routing.
Implement durable claim, snapshot validation, diagnostics and uncertain-output recovery.
Test using synthetic orders and a dedicated test printer; connect UI only after acceptance.
acceptance: Queue-to-spool and physical output, duplicate send, cancellation, offline device and restart tests.

options.title: Disable unsupported kitchen actions in future packaging
options.tradeoff: Reduces misleading UI/API surface; legacy unpaid orders still need a safe resolution path.
steps: Inventory reachable kitchen actions and legacy order handling.
Design a capability gate with a clear unavailable message.
Preserve audited legacy-order resolution and data history.
acceptance: No new unsupported kitchen action is offered; legacy data can still be inspected and resolved.

findings.rollback: Documentation-only scope changes move no data. A future consumer rollback must preserve job history and treat interrupted output as uncertain.
